question: What should I have ready before installing the Veeam Service Provider Console Server component, i.e. what does the setup ask me to provide?
gold_facts: A Microsoft SQL Server to use.

A.text:
Before/during installation, the setup wizard will ask you to provide or confirm the following:

- Acceptance of license agreements [1][6]
- Selection of components to install (Server and/or Web UI) [1][6]
- A license file [1][6]
- A service account (user account and password under which the VSPC services will run and access the database) [1][2][6]
- A system configuration check is performed [1][6]
- Choice of Microsoft SQL Server — use an existing instance or create a new one (default LOCALHOST\VEEAMSQL2017), plus database name and authentication mode/credentials if using SQL authentication [1][2]
- Review of installation settings [1][6]
- Data location [1][6]
- Security certificate (or thumbprint; otherwise a new self-signed certificate is generated) [1][2]
- Ports (e.g., hub port 9999, management port 1989, Web UI port 1280, ConnectWise plugin port 9996 by default) [1][2]
- Final review of the installation summary, including whether to allow automatic product update checks [1][7]

Additionally, before you begin, make sure the machine meets software/hardware requirements, all required ports are open, and (for distributed installs) the Server and Web UI machines can communicate over the network [4].

documents.title: Step 1. Install Veeam Service Provider Console
documents.text:
Step 1. Install Veeam Service Provider Console
Step 1\. Install Veeam Service Provider Console

You can install Veeam Service Provider Console on a physical or virtual machine using a single\-server or a distributed scenario:

* [Single\-server installation scenario](install_onprem_single_server.html)

In this scenario, the Veeam Service Provider Console Server and Web UI structural components are installed on the same machine.

* [Distributed installation scenario](install_onprem_distributed.html)

In this scenario, the Veeam Service Provider Console Server and Web UI structural components are installed on different machines, to separate the client and server roles of the solution.

We recommend to install Veeam Service Provider Console on a dedicated machine to balance the load. However, for small scale and POC deployments, you can install Veeam Service Provider Console on a machine that runs Veeam Cloud Connect.

Before You Begin

Before you begin the installation process, make sure that:

* The machine where you plan to install Veeam Service Provider Console components meets software and hardware requirements.

For details, see [System Requirements](system_requirements.html).

* All required ports are open.

For details, see [Ports](ports.html).

* \[For distributed installation scenario] The machines on which you plan to install Veeam Service Provider Console Server and Web UI components can communicate with each other over the network.

documents.title: Single-Server Installation Scenario
documents.text:
Single-Server Installation Scenario
Single\-Server Installation Scenario

You can install Veeam Service Provider Console on a physical or virtual machine, using the single\-server installation scenario. In this scenario, the Veeam Service Provider Console Server and Web UI components are installed on the same machine. Single\-server scenario is preferable for small\- to medium\-scale deployments.

To install Veeam Service Provider Console using the single\-server installation scenario, perform the following steps:

1. [Launch the splash window](install_launch_splash.html).
2. [Accept license agreements](install_accept_license_agreement.html).
3. [Select components to install](install_select_components.html).
4. [Provide license file](install_provide_license.html).
5. [Specify service account](install_specify_service_account.html).
6. [Perform system configuration check](install_configuration_check.html).
7. [Choose Microsoft SQL server](install_choose_sql_server.html).
8. [Review installation settings](install_review_settings.html).
9. [Specify data location](install_specify_data_location.html).
10. [Select security certificates](install_select_certificate.html).
11. [Specify ports](install_specify_ports.html).
12. [Review installation summary](install_review_summary.html).

documents.title: Step 12. Review Installation Summary
documents.text:
Step 12. Review Installation Summary
Step 12\. Review Installation Summary

At the Ready to Install step of the wizard, review the provided configuration settings.

Select the Allow Veeam Service Provider Console to check for Veeam product updates check box if you want Veeam Service Provider Console to automatically check for available updates. When a new product build is published on the Veeam update server, a notification will be displayed in Veeam Service Provider Console.

Click Install to begin the installation.

[

![Review Installation Settings](/media/8f3e162d-7434-4fe3-8d6d-af80ecba2dbf/d1ecdc0d8e0722e2.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Ready to Install' screen in the Veeam Service Provider Console installer, showing configured installation settings including service user, SQL Server, database name, installation folder, ports, certificate option, license details, and an option to enable product updates. The 'Install' button is highlighted for proceeding with the installation.

](images/setup_server_ready.png "Review Installation Settings")

B.text:
Before installing the Veeam Service Provider Console Server component, the setup asks you to provide:

- A machine that meets the software and hardware requirements [7], and the machine on which the Server component runs must have internet access [12].
- Microsoft SQL Server hosting the Veeam Service Provider Console database, which must be installed on a dedicated machine [5].
- The Veeam Cloud Connect server infrastructure component, which must be installed on a dedicated machine [9], along with a Veeam Cloud Connect license installed on that server [10].
- Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 REST API, which must be installed and activated on the server for the console to communicate with it [4].
- A Veeam ONE setup file from a remote file share, if used — requiring the remote file share location and credentials of an account that Veeam Service Provider Console will use to connect to the file share [11].
- Veeam backup agents setup files, if the Server component machine has no internet connection — these must be delivered to that machine [14]; in offline mode, Veeam Installation Server must be accessed via its API endpoint to download those setup files [3].
- Note that the Server requires certificate validation (access to CRLs) when connecting to Veeam Installation Server to check for new product versions and license updates [1].

documents.title: How to Deploy Veeam Backup Agents in Offline Mode
documents.text:
[How to Deploy Veeam Backup Agents in Offline Mode › How to Deploy Veeam Backup Agents in Offline Mode]
How to Deploy Veeam Backup Agents in Offline Mode
=================================================

If the machine hosting Veeam Service Provider Console Server component has no connection to the internet, you can download Veeam backup agents setup files on machines with internet access and deliver them to the machine where Veeam Service Provider Console Server component is installed.

Step 1\. Disable Automatic Product Updates

Before you install Veeam backup agents in the offline mode, you must disable product updates notifications and download:

1. At the top right corner of the Veeam Service Provider Console window, click Configuration.
2. In the configuration menu on the left, click About.
3. In the Product Updates \& Download section, switch the Automatic checks (recommended) toggle to Off.

Alternatively, you can disable product updates notifications during Veeam Service Provider Console installation. For details, see section [Deploying Veeam Service Provider Console](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vac/deployment/deploy_vac.html?ver=9.2) of the Deployment Guide.

Step 2\. Download Veeam Backup Agents Setup Files

Downloading Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows

To download Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows setup file:

1. Open Veeam Installation Server using the following address: https://vac.butler.veeam.com/api/v2/products/file/update?all\=True\&productName\=vaw\&vspcVersion\=\<vspc\_version\>

where \<vspc\_version\> is the Veeam Service Provider Console build version.

1. For each URL address from the url parameters:

1. Copy URL address from the parameter.
2. Go to the copied address and save the downloaded file.

1. Copy the setup files to a location accessible from the machine where Veeam Service Provider Console Server component is installed.

documents.title: Installing Veeam Cloud Connect License
documents.text:
[Installing Veeam Cloud Connect License › Installing Veeam Cloud Connect License]
Installing Veeam Cloud Connect License
======================================

When you deploy Veeam Service Provider Console, you must install a Veeam Cloud Connect license on the Veeam Cloud Connect server. This can be a free license that comes as part of the Veeam Service Provider Console license file, or a paid license that allows you to expose cloud host and cloud repository resources.

To install a license:


1. Log in to Veeam Service Provider Console.

For details, see [Accessing Veeam Service Provider Console](access_vac.html).

1. At the top right corner of the Veeam Service Provider Console window, click Configuration.
2. In the menu on the left, click License Information.
3. On the Veeam Cloud Connect tab, select Veeam Cloud Connect servers on which you want to install license.

To narrow down the list of Veeam Cloud Connect servers, you can apply the following filters:


* Hostname — search the list of Veeam Cloud Connect servers by the name of the server.
* License status — limit the list of Veeam Cloud Connect servers by status of the installed license (Valid, Warning, Error).

documents.title: Upgrading Veeam ONE Servers
documents.text:
[Upgrading Veeam ONE Servers › Upgrading Veeam ONE Servers]


Before You Begin

Before you start the upgrade procedure, close all Veeam ONE Client instances of the Veeam ONE server that you want to upgrade.

Upgrading Veeam ONE

To upgrade a Veeam ONE server:

1. Log in to Veeam Service Provider Console.

For details, see [Accessing Veeam Service Provider Console](access_vac.html).

1. In the menu on the left, click Discovery (for Service Provider Global Administrator, Service Provider Administrator) or Managed Computers (for Service Provider Operator).
2. Open the ONE Servers tab.
3. Select the necessary computers in the list.
4. At the top of the list, click Manage Updates and choose Upgrade Server.

Alternatively, you can right\-click the necessary server, select Manage Updates and choose Upgrade Server.

Veeam Service Provider Console will open the Upgrade Veeam ONE wizard.

1. At the Source step of the wizard, specify the location of the Veeam ONE distribution:

* To use a latest distribution from Veeam License Update server, select the Download the Veeam ONE setup file from a Veeam web server option.
* To use a distribution stored on a remote file share, select the Use the Veeam ONE setup file from the remote file share option and specify remote file share location and credentials of an account that Veeam Service Provider Console will use to connect to the file share.

* If you have previously downloaded an installation file to the remote computer, select the Use a previously downloaded installation file option. Veeam Service Provider Console will locate the downloaded installation file automatically.

For details on how to download the installation file in Veeam Service Provider Console, see [Downloading Setup File](#download_iso).

documents.title: Veeam Intelligence
documents.text:
[Veeam Intelligence › Veeam Intelligence]

Limitations of Veeam Intelligence

Veeam Intelligence has the following limitations:

* The machine on which Veeam Service Provider Console Server component runs must have internet access.
* Network access with the following conditions is required for the machines on which your workstation web browser and Veeam Service Provider Console Server runs:

* An open connection to rest\-ai.veeam.com, cdn.rest\-ai.veeam.com and js.veeam.com
* An HTTPS port configured during setup (by default, port 1280 is used)
* Protocols used to communicate Veeam Intelligence queries: HTTPS and WSS (transport level: TCP)

Network communication between your workstation web browser, Veeam Service Provider Console Server component and the Veeam AI Service is displayed in the following schema:

[

![Veeam Intelligence Ports](/media/fb66dc75-5eb8-4abc-b4bb-16b8b2f7bc9d/687f6e56b7a0.png)

> **Figure:** Diagram showing the communication flow between Veeam Service Provider Console Server, Veeam Service Provider Console Web UI, Veeam CDN, and Veeam AI Service. Connections use HTTPS port 1280 for downloading JS and signature manifests, authentication, and direct chat with the bot. The Console Server connects to the Web UI via a configurable HTTPS port (default 1280).

](images/ai_ports.png "Veeam Intelligence Ports")

question: We want to roll out Veeam Recon for Veeam Infrastructure. Which licence editions include it, how many machines can it run on at once, and how many extra people can I give access to the Coveware portal?
gold_facts: Recon is included in the Advanced and Premium editions of the Veeam Data Platform Universal License.
Recon is not supported with Veeam Data Platform Essentials.
Recon can be installed and run simultaneously on up to 10 endpoints.
Up to 15 additional users can be added in the Coveware account (Settings > Users > Add User).

A.text:
Recon for Veeam Infrastructure is included in the Advanced and Premium editions of the Veeam Data Platform Universal License [1][3]. For Veeam Data Platform Essentials, the solution is not supported [3].

Regarding machine coverage: version 3.0 provides expanded coverage to install on up to 10 servers within Veeam Data Platform, including backup repositories, proxies, gateways, and Active Directory servers [6]. (The earlier v2.1 supported up to 5 such servers [4].)

For user access, Recon for Veeam Infrastructure provides user addition of up to 15 additional users in the Coveware account [2].

sources.paraphrase: Recon for Veeam Infrastructure is included in the Advanced and Premium edition of the Veeam Data Platform Universal License.

Firewall Rules

If you have strict firewall rules, add the following outbound connections to the allowlist.

| From | To | Protocol | Port | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Machine with Recon | *update.coveware.com* | TCP | 443 | Used to get updates for Recon. |
| * *auth.api.coveware.com* * *coveware\-recon\-results.s3\.amazonaws.com* * *coveware\-sample\-verifications.s3\.amazonaws.com* | TCP | 443 | Used to communicate with the Recon REST API and upload scan results. |

For Amazon connections, you can also add to the allowlist `us-east-1` IP ranges instead of domain names. For more information, see [this Amazon article](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/aws-ip-ranges.html#filter-json-file).

Activating Solution

To activate Recon for Veeam Infrastructure, perform the following steps:

1. Log in to [your Veeam account](https://www.veeam.com/services/auth/login).

| Note |
| --- |
| The account must have one of the following roles assigned: *Primary License Administrator*, *Secondary License Administrator*, *License Administrator*, *Primary Account Administrator*, *Secondary Account Administrator*, or *Cross\-Account Administrator*. |

2. Click **My Account** \> **Products**.
3. In the **Product downloads** section, select *Recon* and click **Activate**.

After you activate the solution, you will receive an email to set up your Coveware account. If there is an issue with the email delivery, contact Coveware Support.

documents.title: System Requirements
documents.text:
[System Requirements › System Requirements]

October 2025

Recon for Veeam Infrastructure integrated with Veeam App for Microsoft Sentinel. You can now track Veeam events and security activities found with Recon directly in your Microsoft Sentinel workspace.

For more information, see [Veeam App for Microsoft Sentinel User Guide](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/security_plugins_microsoft_sentinel/guide/intro.html?ver=1).

July 2025

The Triage Inbox section added to the Coveware portal. Key features:

* **Enhanced Visibility:** Instantly access and review suspicious events, ensuring potential threats never go unnoticed.
* **Risk\-Based Filtering:** Prioritize your response by filtering events according to their risk level.
* **Actionable Context:** Gain deeper insights into suspicious activity with direct links to relevant MITRE ATT\&CK® information, helping you understand and respond faster.


March 2025

Recon for Veeam Infrastructure v2\.1 released:

* **Expanded Coverage:** You can install Recon on up to 5 servers within Veeam Data Platform including backup repositories, proxies, gateways, and Active Directory servers.
* **Linux Support:** Recon is now compatible with all modern Linux distributions, making for easier installation and support.
* **Enhanced Features:** User access management, email notification settings, a new endpoint overview page, direct proxy access, and more.
